#### **3.1.7 Non-Screen Functions** {#3.1.7-non-screen-functions}

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Inbound Management | Landed Cost Allocation Engine | Automatically distributes additional expenses (e.g., shipping, handling, customs fees) across the imported items based on user-selected criteria (by item value or quantity/weight) upon inbound confirmation. |
| 2 | Inbound Management | MAC Recalculation Service | Recalculates the Moving Average Cost (MAC) of the received products when a goods receipt is completed, and on other inbound movements, through the shared inventory ledger. |
| 3 | Production Management | BOM Material Requirement Calculator | Calculates the material requirement of production orders and plans from the active BOM: Planned Quantity × Standard Quantity × (1 \+ Wastage Rate), and the shortage against stock. |
| 4 | Sales & Outbound | Customer Credit Validator | Checks Current Debt \+ Expected New Debt ≤ Credit Limit when a POS invoice is paid; the transaction is blocked unless the Manager has approved a credit request or the debt-warning settings allow debt over the limit. |
| 5 | Sales & Outbound | Partial Delivery of Bookings | When an invoice delivers less than the remaining quantity of a booking, the booking stays in Delivering with the remaining quantity instead of creating a new order. |
| 6 | Inventory Control | Reorder & Expiry Alert (Cron Job) | A scheduled background process (e.g., running every hour or nightly) that scans current inventory balances and batch expiration dates, subsequently pushing alerts to the Manager and Warehouse dashboards. |
| 7 | Returns & Finance | Debt Auto-Adjustment | Updates customer debt and supplier payable whenever an invoice, receipt, return, voucher or debt adjustment is completed or cancelled; vouchers are allocated to the oldest unpaid documents first. |
| 8 | Account & Security | Audit Trail Logging Service | Asynchronously records critical system events (e.g., stock adjustments, credit limit modifications, manual status overrides) into a secure log database, capturing User ID, timestamp, action type, and before/after values for compliance tracking. |
| 9 | System Utilities | Automated DB Backup (Cron Job) | A scheduled maintenance job that performs a full backup of the system's database to prevent data loss, ensuring the recovery of enterprise data in case of system failure. |
| 10 | Inventory Control | Inventory Ledger | Every stock movement updates the inventory balance by warehouse, location, product and lot and appends a stock card line (type, reference, user) in the same transaction. |
| 11 | System Utilities | Document Code Generator | Generates document codes from database sequences using the prefixes and rule (sequential, date-time, random) of the order settings. |
| 12 | Account & Security | Permission & Warehouse Isolation Check | On every request, reads the permissions of the user's role and the assigned warehouses from the database; locked users have no permission. |
| 13 | Inventory Control | Stocktake Transaction Guard | Blocks material issues, finished goods receipts, completion approvals and disposals of items that are in a Draft stocktake of the same warehouse. |

#### **3.1.8 Entity Relationship Diagram** {#3.1.8-entity-relationship-diagram}

**Entities Description**

| \# | Entity | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | BomItem | BOM material lines: standard quantity, unit, wastage rate. |
| 2 | GoodsReceiptItem | Lines of a goods receipt (quantity, cost, lot, location). |
| 3 | InboundCostAllocation | Allocation of landed cost to receipt lines (table exists, no processing code yet). |
| 4 | InventoryDisposalItem | Lines of a disposal (product, quantity, cost, reason). |
| 5 | OrderItem | Lines of a booking or invoice (product, unit, quantity, price, discount). |
| 6 | PriceBookItem | Price of one product in a price book. |
| 7 | ProductionOrderItem | Finished goods lines of a production order (multi-product orders). |
| 8 | ProductionPlanItem | Plan lines: finished good, planned quantity, period, receiving warehouse. |
| 9 | PurchaseOrderItem | Lines of a purchase order. |
| 10 | PurchaseReturnItem | Lines of a purchase return. |
| 11 | ReturnRequestItem | Lines of a sales return (returned quantity, return price, sale price). |
| 12 | StockIssueItem | Lines of a stock issue (product, lot, quantity, linked order line or material requirement). |
| 13 | StockTransferItem | Lines of a transfer (dispatched and received quantity, transfer price). |
| 14 | StocktakeItem | Lines of a stocktake (system quantity, counted quantity, discrepancy). |
| 15 | RolePermission | Links a role to its permission codes (module permissions and feature permissions). |
| 16 | UserRole | Links an account to its role (one role per account in the current build). |
| 17 | UserWarehouseAccess | Warehouses an account may access (data isolation, BR-04). |
| 18 | Bom | Bill of materials per finished good with version and active flag. |
| 19 | BusinessPartner | Customers and suppliers in one table (partner\_type): contact data, credit limit, current debt / payable, active flag. |
| 20 | DebtWarningSetting | Single-row debt warning settings: amount threshold, days threshold, allow debt over limit, default credit limit. |
| 21 | InventoryLot | Lot numbers with manufacturing and expiry dates. |
| 22 | OrderSetting | Single-row system settings: document code prefixes and rules, return time limit, allow negative stock, default credit limit. |
| 23 | PriceBook | Price books: scope (branch, customer group, customer type, user), formula based on another price book. |
| 24 | ProductCategory | Product categories. |
| 25 | ProductImage | Product images (several per product, one primary). |
| 26 | Product | Goods, raw materials and finished goods: code, name, type, base unit, prices, reorder point, moving average cost, active flag. |
| 27 | UnitConversion | Conversion factors between units (table exists, not used by documents yet). |
| 28 | Unit | Units of measure. |
| 29 | WarehouseLocation | Storage locations inside a warehouse. |
| 30 | Warehouse | Warehouses / branches (code, name, address, active flag). |
| 31 | Permission | Permission codes: MODULE\_ACTION codes and FEAT\_\* feature codes (navigation items). |
| 32 | Role | Roles. The role code is stored with the description in the current build. |
| 33 | User | Employee accounts (username, password hash, contact data, active flag). |
| 34 | CreditLimitHistory | History of changes of a customer credit limit (old limit, new limit, reason). |
| 35 | CreditLimitRequest | Credit requests raised from POS: one-time exception or new limit, status PENDING / APPROVED / REJECTED. |
| 36 | FinancialTransaction | Vouchers: customer receipts, supplier payments, refunds, debt adjustments. |
| 37 | FinishedGoodsReceipt | Finished goods receipts into the finished goods warehouse. |
| 38 | GoodsReceipt | Goods receipts from suppliers (DRAFT, COMPLETED, CANCELLED); PO reference optional. |
| 39 | InboundCost | Landed cost header (table exists, no processing code yet). |
| 40 | InventoryBalance | Stock on hand by warehouse, location, product and lot. |
| 41 | InventoryDisposal | Disposal documents (DRAFT, COMPLETED, CANCELLED). |
| 42 | InventoryTransaction | Stock card: every stock movement with type, reference document and user. |
| 43 | Order | Sales documents. order\_type BOOKING (customer order, reserves quantity) or INVOICE (POS invoice). Status, totals, paid / deposit amounts, link to booking and merged order. |
| 44 | ProductionMaterialRequirement | Material requirement snapshot of an order: required, issued, shortage; norm adjustments with reason. |
| 45 | ProductionOrder | Production orders (NOT\_STARTED, IN\_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, CANCELLED), optionally linked to a plan. |
| 46 | ProductionPlan | Production plans (DRAFT, PENDING\_APPROVAL, APPROVED, REJECTED, CLOSED, CANCELLED). |
| 47 | ProductionReport | Production reports: good and defective quantities. |
| 48 | PurchaseOrder | Purchase orders to suppliers (DRAFT, ORDERED, PARTIAL, COMPLETED, CANCELLED). |
| 49 | PurchaseReturn | Purchase returns to suppliers, created after a goods receipt, with refunds. |
| 50 | ReturnProcessing | Processing record of a returned line (restocking). |
| 51 | ReturnRequest | Sales returns (customer returns) referencing an invoice. |
| 52 | StockIssue | Stock issue documents created with invoices and production material issues. |
| 53 | StockTransfer | Stock transfers between warehouses (DRAFT, IN\_TRANSIT, RECEIVED, CANCELLED). |
| 54 | Stocktake | Stocktakes (DRAFT, BALANCED, CANCELLED) for one warehouse. |

### **3.2 Functional Specifications** {#3.2-functional-specifications}

#### **3.2.0 Login** {#3.2.0-login}

![][image17]  
**Description:**

This screen allows an employee to sign in to StockFlow.

**Main Features:**

Accepts the username (or email or employee code) and the password, shows the error message on failure and opens the first screen permitted to the role.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Username | Username, email or employee code of the account (required) |
| Password | Password with show/hide toggle (required) |
| Login Button | Validates the credentials and the account status, then opens the application |
| Error Message | Generic message when the username or password is wrong, or when the account is locked |

#### **3.2.1 Admin** {#3.2.1-admin}

##### **3.2.1.1 Admin Dashboard**

**Description:**

This screen is the landing page of the Admin with an overview of accounts, roles and warehouses and shortcuts to the administration screens.

**Main Features:**

Shows the number of employees (active), roles and warehouse facilities and opens Employees, Roles, Role Matrix and Warehouse Access; opens Change Password.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Total Employees Card | Number of employee accounts and active accounts, with View List shortcut |
| Roles Card | Number of roles with Configure Roles shortcut |
| Warehouse Facilities Card | Number of warehouses with Warehouse Access shortcut |
| Detailed Permissions Shortcut | Opens the Role Matrix |
| Change Password Button | Opens the Change Password popup |

##### **3.2.1.2 Change Password \<\<Popup\>\>**

![][image18]  
**Description:**

This popup allows a logged-in user to change his or her own password.

**Main Features:**

Enter the current password, the new password and the confirmation; the strength checklist is updated while typing.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Current Password | Password currently in use (required) |
| New Password | New password (required) |
| Confirm Password | Must match the new password |
| Password Standard | Checklist: at least 8 characters, uppercase, lowercase, digit, special character |
| Update Password Button | Validates and saves the new password |
| Cancel Button | Closes the popup without changes |

##### **3.2.1.3 Employee Account List**

![][image19]  
**Description:**

This screen displays all employee accounts and the actions on them.

**Main Features:**

Search by name, employee code or email; filter by status and role; add, edit, lock/unlock an account and reset its password.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Search Input | Searches by name, employee code or email |
| Status Filter | All statuses, Active, Locked |
| Role Filter | All roles or one role |
| Add Employee Button | Opens the Create Account form |
| Employee Table | Employee code, full name, contact, role, assigned warehouses, status, actions |
| Status Badge | Active or Locked |
| Edit Action | Opens the Update Account form |
| Lock / Unlock Action | Changes the status of the account after confirmation |
| Reset Password Action | Resets the password to the default password |

##### **3.2.1.4 Create / Update Account Form \<\<Popup\>\>**

![][image20]  
**Description:**

This popup allows the Admin to create or update an employee account.

**Main Features:**

Enter personal data, username, role and warehouses; the employee code is generated when left empty; checks duplicate username, email and employee code.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Avatar | Employee photo (JPG, PNG, WEBP); upload or remove |
| Employee Code | Optional; generated automatically when empty; must be unique |
| Full Name | Required |
| Username | Login name of the account; required and unique |
| Phone Number | Required |
| Email | Valid email format; unique |
| Job Title | Job title of the employee |
| Role | One role: Manager, Sales, Warehouse, Production or a custom role |
| Assigned Warehouses | Warehouses the account may access |
| Save / Cancel Buttons | Save the account or close the popup |

##### **3.2.1.5 Role List & Create Form**

![][image21]  
**Description:**

This screen displays the roles and allows the Admin to create, update and delete roles.

**Main Features:**

List roles with their accounts; create a custom role; edit the description; delete a role that no account holds.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Role Cards | Role name, code, description and number of accounts; System badge for default roles |
| Create Role Button | Opens the Add Role popup |
| Role Name | Required; the name of a default system role cannot be changed |
| Role Code | Normalized to uppercase with prefix ROLE\_ |
| Role Description | Responsibilities of the role |
| Configure Permissions Action | Opens the Role Matrix for the role |
| Delete Role Action | Deletes the role after confirmation; blocked while accounts hold it |

##### **3.2.1.6 Configure Permissions (Role Matrix)**

![][image22]  
**Description:**

This screen displays the navbar features by role and allows the Admin to grant or remove them.

**Main Features:**

Tick or untick each feature for each role; the module permissions of the role are derived from the ticked features; default roles can be reset to their defaults.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Search Input | Searches features |
| Feature Column | Navbar features grouped by menu (Overview, Employees, Permissions, Goods, Customers, Sales, Purchasing, Production, BOM) |
| Role Columns | One checkbox per role and feature |
| Totals | Total number of features and roles |
| Default Button | Restores the default features of a role |
| Save Button | Saves the matrix |

##### **3.2.1.7 Warehouse Access List**

![][image23]  
**Description:**

This screen displays the warehouses assigned to each employee and the warehouse facilities.

**Main Features:**

Filter by warehouse, search employees, assign warehouses to an employee, add or edit a warehouse facility.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Warehouse Filter | All warehouses or one warehouse |
| Search Input | Searches employees by name or employee code |
| Access Table | Employee code, employee, department, role, assigned warehouses, actions |
| Warehouse Access Action | Opens the Assign Warehouse Access popup |
| Add Warehouse Button | Opens the warehouse facility form |

##### **3.2.1.8 Assign Warehouse Access \<\<Popup\>\>**

![][image24]  
**Description:**

This popup allows the Admin to choose the warehouses an employee may access.

**Main Features:**

Shows the active warehouses as a checklist and saves the selection.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Employee | Name and code of the selected employee |
| Warehouse Checklist | Active warehouses with checkboxes |
| Save Access Button | Saves the warehouse access |
| Cancel Button | Closes the popup |

##### **3.2.1.9 Warehouse Facility Form \<\<Popup\>\>**

![][image25]  
**Description:**

This popup allows the Admin to add or update a warehouse.

**Main Features:**

Enter the warehouse code, name, address and area; the new warehouse appears in the access list.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Warehouse Code | Generated automatically (K00X) or entered; must be unique |
| Warehouse Name | Required |
| Warehouse Address | Address of the warehouse |
| Area / Scale | Area of the warehouse |

##### **3.2.1.10 Order Settings**

**Description:**

This screen allows the Admin to configure order and transaction rules.

**Main Features:**

Configure bookings, sales & POS, returns, transaction time and document code rules; only the Admin can save.

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Group A – Bookings | Accept new bookings; allow bookings when out of stock; use quantities held for other bookings; allow moving a booking to another branch |
| Group B – Sales & POS | Allow selling below stock (negative stock); show quotation printing; confirmation before completing a POS transaction |
| Group C – Returns | Limit the return period and the maximum number of days |
| Group D – Transaction Time | Lock the transaction date to real time |
| Group E – Code Rules | Code format: sequential, date-time or random; prefixes of invoice (HD), booking (DH), return (TH), transfer (CK) and other documents |
| Save / Reload Buttons | Save the settings or reload them |

##### **3.2.5.1 Purchase Order List & Form**

## **4\. Non-Functional Requirements** {#4.-non-functional-requirements}

### **4.1 External Interfaces** {#4.1-external-interfaces}

* **User Interfaces:** StockFlow shall provide a desktop web interface (minimum resolution 1366×768) for the Admin, Manager, Sales Accountant, Warehouse Accountant and Production Accountant. Each user shall see only the functions granted to his or her role and only data of the assigned warehouses. Forms shall provide clear validation messages, confirmation prompts, status indicators and search/filter functions; the interface and system messages are in Vietnamese.

* **Hardware Interfaces:** No special hardware is required. StockFlow runs on standard desktop/laptop computers with a web browser and a standard office printer for printing documents (invoices, purchase orders, receipts, transfer and stocktake notes). Barcode scanners and mobile devices are not supported.

* **Software Interfaces:** StockFlow consists of a web front end and a REST/JSON API with token authentication, and stores transactional and master data in a PostgreSQL relational database. StockFlow does not integrate with external accounting software (e.g. MISA) or banks; all amounts are kept as net values excluding VAT, and VAT calculation and electronic invoicing are outside the scope of the system.

* **Integration Boundary:** Customers, suppliers and field staff (warehouse checkers, foremen, team leaders, workers) shall not access StockFlow. Their information is entered by authorized office staff based on paper documents and count reports.

### **4.2 Quality Attributes** {#4.2-quality-attributes}

The system must provide a usable, responsive, reliable, secure, maintainable, and traceable environment for Tín Phát's internal order, inventory, warehouse, purchasing, sales, and production operations.

#### **4.2.1 Usability** {#4.2.1-usability}

* **Learnability:** A new Admin, Manager, Sales Accountant, Warehouse Accountant or Production Accountant should be able to complete the common tasks of his or her role (account management, bookings and POS sales, goods receipt, transfer, stocktake, production material issue and finished goods receipt) after a short orientation.

* **Consistency:** All list screens follow the same layout (filter sidebar, search box, table with expandable detail, pagination) and common actions such as Save Draft, Complete, Cancel, Copy, Export, Print, Approve and Reject use consistent labels.

* **Error Prevention:** Required fields, stock quantities, warehouse selection, credit limits, production quantities, transaction status, and irreversible actions shall be clearly indicated and validated before confirmation.

* **Operational Clarity:** Booking, invoice, purchase, transfer, stocktake, disposal, production and approval statuses shall be clearly displayed so users can understand the current state of a transaction.

* **Accessibility:** The interface should provide readable text, adequate contrast, keyboard shortcuts in data-entry screens (e.g. F3 search, F4 customer) and appropriately labeled form controls.

#### **4.2.2 Performance** {#4.2.2-performance}

* **Normal Page Response:** For typical operations under expected load, 95% of normal non-report requests should complete within 2 seconds, excluding client network latency.

* **Transaction Response:** Common transactional operations such as saving bookings, completing POS invoices, completing goods receipts, recording production issues and receipts, and completing stocktakes should normally return confirmation within 3 seconds under expected load.

* **Search Response:** Product, material, order, customer and inventory searches should normally return results within 2 seconds.

* **Report Response:** Standard inventory, sales, debt, cost, profit, purchasing, and production reports should normally render within 5 seconds for the expected project dataset. Large exports may be processed asynchronously when necessary.

* **Concurrency:** The baseline deployment should support at least 100 concurrently authenticated internal users without functional degradation, with capacity adjustable according to deployment resources.

#### **4.2.3 Reliability** {#4.2.3-reliability}

* **Availability:** The deployed system should target at least 99.5% monthly availability, excluding planned maintenance.

* **Data Integrity:** Inventory quantities, customer debt, supplier payable, production progress, and transaction statuses must remain transactionally consistent and must not create invalid duplicate or conflicting records.

* **Inventory Consistency:** Stock quantities must only be changed after the corresponding business transaction is successfully committed. Every stock change updates the inventory balance and the stock card in the same database transaction; a failed transaction must not partially update inventory.

* **Transaction Recovery:** If a save or confirmation operation fails, the system must display a clear error and must not report the transaction as completed unless the database transaction has been successfully committed. Repeated clicks on payment must not create duplicate invoices.

* **Backup and Recovery:** Application and database data should be backed up at least daily, and restoration procedures should be documented and tested during the project.

* **Stocktake Protection:** While a stocktake is in Draft, material issues, finished goods receipts and disposals of the items in its scope in that warehouse shall not be confirmed (BR-42).

#### **4.2.4 Security & Privacy** {#4.2.4-security-&-privacy}

* **Access Control:** Every protected API endpoint and screen must enforce role-based authorization and warehouse-level data isolation. Hiding a UI control alone shall not be considered sufficient authorization.

* **Role-Based Access Control:** Each account holds one role; the Admin configures the functions of each role. Permissions are read from the database on every request, so changes apply immediately.

* **Warehouse Data Isolation:** Employees shall only access and operate on warehouse data for warehouses assigned to their accounts.

* **Credential Protection:** Passwords must be stored using a modern salted adaptive password-hashing algorithm. Plaintext passwords must never be stored.

* **Transport Security:** Production web traffic shall use HTTPS/TLS.

* **Session Security:** Sessions use signed tokens with a fixed lifetime; a locked account loses its permissions at the next request, and the user is returned to the login screen when the token is rejected.

* **Financial Data Protection:** Financial information, customer debt, supplier payable, cost, revenue, profit, and payment-related data shall only be accessible to authorized roles.

* **Auditability:** Security-sensitive and material administrative operations, including account-status changes, role/permission changes, warehouse-access changes, credit-limit changes, inventory adjustments, and other controlled operations should generate audit records containing the responsible user, timestamp, action, and relevant before/after values.

* **Approval Traceability:** Every approval or rejection (credit request, production plan, stocktake adjustment, disposal) shall record the approver, time and note (BR-50).

#### **4.2.5 Maintainability & Compatibility** {#4.2.5-maintainability-&-compatibility}

* **Modularity:** Authentication and authorization, master data, purchasing and receiving, sales and order management, warehouse/inventory control, production management, returns and finance should be separated into maintainable modules (Clean Architecture back end, feature-based front end).

* **Configuration:** Warehouses, units and conversions, BOM/material norms, price books, customer credit limits, debt warnings, reorder points, order settings, role permissions, and other configurable business parameters should be maintained through the system without source-code changes where practical.

* **Browser Compatibility:** The web interface should support current stable desktop versions of Chrome, Edge and Firefox.

* **Screen Layout:** The interface is designed for desktop screens; data-entry screens (POS, receipts, transfers, stocktake grids) should support fast keyboard entry and import from Excel.

* **Logging and Diagnostics:** Server-side errors and important system events must be logged with sufficient technical context for troubleshooting while avoiding unnecessary exposure of customer, employee, and financial data.

* **Module Independence:** Business rules (credit check, MAC calculation, BOM requirement, stock isolation) should be implemented in the service layer, independent of the user interface, so that rules can change without redesigning screens.

* **Data Consistency and Versioning:** Changes to master data, configuration, and business transactions should preserve sufficient history (stock card, debt history, credit limit history) to support troubleshooting, operational traceability, and future system maintenance.

## **5\. Requirement Appendix** {#5.-requirement-appendix}

### **5.1 Business Rules** {#5.1-business-rules}

| ID | Rule Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| **BR-01** | Only Active accounts can log in. Username, employee code and email must each identify exactly one account; any of them can be used to log in. |
| **BR-02** | Every function is controlled by permissions (RBAC). Each account holds one role; its permissions are the functions granted to that role. Authorization is checked on the server for every request, using the permissions stored in the database, not only by hiding UI controls. |
| **BR-03** | Only the Admin can create or update roles, add or remove functions of a role, set the role of an account, assign warehouses to an account and maintain warehouses. Every account has exactly one role. Default system roles cannot be renamed and a role held by accounts cannot be deleted. |
| **BR-04** | A user can view and process warehouse data (inventory, receipts, issues, transfers, stocktakes, returns, disposals) only for the warehouses assigned to his or her account. This rule applies to all roles, including the Manager. |
| **BR-05** | Passwords must have at least 8 characters including uppercase, lowercase, digit and special character and are stored only as salted hashes. A session token is valid for a fixed period; a locked account loses all permissions at its next request. |
| **BR-06** | Codes that must be unique (product, partner, warehouse, order, voucher codes...) must not be duplicated. Master data used by any transaction cannot be deleted, only deactivated. |
| **BR-07** | Customers and suppliers do not use StockFlow. Their orders, deliveries and payments are entered by authorized employees. |
| **BR-08** | Customer orders received by phone, Zalo or in person are entered by the Sales Accountant as bookings. Creating, updating or canceling a booking does not change inventory; the booked quantity is shown as reserved ("customer ordered"). |
| **BR-09** | Only bookings that have not been delivered (Draft or Confirmed) can be updated or canceled. Bookings that are not Cancelled or Finished can be consolidated or processed into an invoice. |
| **BR-10** | Only bookings of the same customer and the same processing warehouse can be consolidated into one booking. The source bookings are cancelled and linked to the new booking. |
| **BR-11** | The unit price of an order line is taken from the applicable price book (by default the general price book) and may be adjusted by the Sales Accountant. All prices and amounts are net values (excluding VAT). |
| **BR-12** | A sales invoice can be completed only if Current Debt \+ (Invoice Total − Paid Amount) ≤ Credit Limit, or if the Manager has approved a credit request for the customer, or if the debt-warning settings allow debt over the limit. |
| **BR-13** | Credit requests are decided by the Manager (consulting the Director when required by company policy). The Manager may approve a one-time exception for the transaction, approve a new credit limit, or reject. No interest is charged on customer debt. |
| **BR-14** | The paid amount of a transaction must be between 0 and the total value. A bank transfer payment must have a bank reference. A payment QR code must contain the exact paid amount and the transaction code. The paid amount is recorded as a customer receipt. |
| **BR-15** | Customer receivable increases by the unpaid amount of a sales invoice when the invoice is completed, and decreases by receipts, completed returns and debt adjustments. Cancelling a document reverses its effect. |
| **BR-16** | The quantity of an invoice line must not exceed the available stock (on-hand quantity minus quantities reserved by other bookings) unless negative stock is allowed in the order settings. Inventory is deducted by the invoiced quantity when the invoice is completed. |
| **BR-17** | If an invoice delivers less than the remaining quantity of a booking, the booking becomes Delivering and keeps the remaining quantity; it becomes Finished when everything is delivered or when the Sales Accountant finishes it. |
| **BR-18** | The due date of a receivable is the stock issue date plus the customer's payment term (days). Receivables unpaid after the due date are overdue. |
| **BR-19** | A sales return must reference a Completed invoice, except a quick return without invoice. The return quantity must not exceed the invoiced quantity minus the quantity already returned. |
| **BR-20** | Each returned item must be categorized: Restock (added to available inventory), Repair (held in the warehouse as Under Repair, not available, until the repair result is Restock or Scrap) or Scrap (Waiting for Disposal). |
| **BR-21** | When a return is completed, the returned goods are added back to inventory and the customer debt is reduced by the return value minus the return fee. Money paid back to the customer is recorded as a refund on the return. |
| **BR-22** | A purchase order must have a supplier, a receiving warehouse and at least one item with quantity \> 0 and unit price ≥ 0\. Only purchase orders without any receipt can be updated or canceled; purchase orders of the same supplier and warehouse can be merged. |
| **BR-23** | A goods receipt may reference a purchase order in status Ordered or Partially Received. When the receipt is completed, the purchase order becomes Partially Received or Completed according to the received quantities. |
| **BR-24** | Only accepted quantities are added to inventory and paid. Defective quantities are recorded on the receipt line, are not added to inventory and are not paid. Goods can be returned to the supplier by a purchase return referencing the receipt. |
| **BR-25** | Supplier payable increases by the unpaid amount of a completed receipt (accepted quantity × unit price − discounts − paid amount) and decreases by payment vouchers, purchase returns and debt adjustments. |
| **BR-26** | Quantities entered in another unit are converted to the product's base unit using the configured conversion factor. |
| **BR-27** | For products tracked by lot/expiry, the lot number and expiry date must be entered when the goods are received. |
| **BR-28** | Landed costs are allocated only to items of a Completed goods receipt, by value or by quantity. The total allocated amount must equal the total landed cost. |
| **BR-29** | Moving Average Cost is recalculated at each confirmed purchase receipt and each landed cost allocation: New MAC \= (On-hand Qty × Current MAC \+ Added Cost) / (On-hand Qty \+ Added Qty). |
| **BR-30** | A production order can be created only for a finished good that has an Active BOM. Each finished good has at most one Active BOM version. A new production order follows the active BOM; norms are changed only by adjusting an existing order (BR-51). |
| **BR-31** | Material requirement \= Planned Quantity × Standard Quantity per Unit × (1 \+ Wastage Rate). It is calculated by the system from the BOM, not entered manually. |
| **BR-32** | Every material issue must reference a production order code. Supplementary issues use the same code. The system keeps the cumulative issued quantity and the shortage (Required − Issued, minimum 0\) of each material. |
| **BR-33** | Material inventory is deducted by the actual issued quantity confirmed by the Production Accountant. The issued quantity must not exceed the available stock. |
| **BR-34** | A supplementary issue that makes the cumulative issued quantity exceed the requirement must have a reason. |
| **BR-35** | The finished goods quantity is recorded from the warehouse checker's count. If the cumulative received quantity exceeds the planned quantity, the system asks for confirmation before saving. |
| **BR-36** | Accepted finished goods are added to the finished goods warehouse when the receipt is confirmed. Defective finished goods are recorded separately and are not added to sellable inventory. |
| **BR-37** | If the received finished goods need more material than has been issued according to the BOM, the system shows a warning, requires a note and flags the receipt for the Manager; the receipt is not blocked. |
| **BR-38** | Production order status: Not Started → In Progress (first material issue) → Completed (the Manager approves completion, or the received quantity reaches the planned quantity) or closed early by the Manager with a reason. Only Not Started orders can be updated or canceled. |
| **BR-39** | Production Accountants cannot view purchase prices, costs, MAC or selling prices. |
| **BR-40** | A transfer must have different source and destination warehouses and at least one item. The source inventory is reduced at dispatch (In Transit); the destination inventory is increased by the received quantity at receipt (Received). Cancelling a dispatched transfer restores the source inventory. |
| **BR-41** | If the received quantity of a transfer line is lower than the transferred quantity, the destination warehouse must enter a receiving note explaining the shortage. |
| **BR-42** | While a stocktake of a warehouse is in Draft, material issues, finished goods receipts, completion approvals and disposals of the items in its scope in that warehouse cannot be confirmed. |
| **BR-43** | Every stocktake line with a variance must have a reason. Inventory is adjusted to the counted quantity only after the Manager approves; the Manager may also reject or request a recount. |
| **BR-44** | A disposal must have a quantity not exceeding the available quantity and a reason. Inventory is reduced only after the Manager approves. |
| **BR-45** | All amounts in StockFlow are net values excluding VAT. VAT calculation and electronic invoicing are outside the scope of StockFlow. |
| **BR-46** | A voucher amount must be greater than 0 and not greater than the outstanding balance. Confirmed vouchers cannot be edited; a mistake is corrected by a reversing voucher. |
| **BR-47** | Reports are generated only from confirmed transactions. |
| **BR-48** | A reorder alert is raised when the on-hand quantity is at or below the product's reorder point. An expiry alert is raised for lots expiring within the configured number of days or already expired. |
| **BR-49** | Changes of accounts, roles, permissions, warehouse access, credit limits, credit decisions, inventory adjustments, disposals and vouchers are recorded in the audit trail with user, time, action and before/after values. |
| **BR-50** | Every approval decision records the approver, time and note. A rejection must have a reason. |
| **BR-51** | The Manager may adjust the material norms of an open production order with a reason. Only that order is changed, not the BOM; the new requirement of a material cannot be lower than its issued quantity. |
| **BR-52** | A material can be removed from a production order only if nothing has been issued for it. |
| **BR-PP-01 – BR-PP-08** | A production plan has a system-generated unique code, a name, a period and at least one line. Each line has a finished or semi-finished good that is active, a quantity \> 0 and dates inside the plan period; a product appears once per plan. The receiving warehouse is optional and must be active and accessible. Planning does not change inventory or reserve materials. |
| **BR-PP-09 – BR-PP-15** | A plan can be submitted and approved only if every finished good has an active BOM. Draft and Rejected plans can be fully edited; an Approved plan can change only quantities (not below the ordered quantity), dates, warehouse and note. The estimated requirement is calculated from the BOM and is not stored; a material shortage is only a warning. |
| **BR-PP-16 – BR-PP-21** | Production orders can be created only from an Approved plan. The quantity ordered for a finished good must not exceed the remaining quantity (planned − ordered, excluding cancelled orders). A plan can have many orders; an order belongs to at most one plan. |
| **BR-PP-22 – BR-PP-24** | A rejection must have a reason; the approver and approval time are recorded. A plan with orders that are not cancelled cannot be cancelled and must be closed instead. Closing or cancelling a plan does not change its orders; plans are never deleted. |

| 56 | MSG56 | Toast (Success) | Approval recorded | Your decision has been recorded. |
| 57 | MSG57 | Toast (Error) | Already decided | This request has already been processed. |
| 58 | MSG58 | Inline (Error) | No active BOM | The selected product has no active BOM. Please configure the BOM first. |
| 59 | MSG59 | Inline (Error) | Invalid voucher amount | Amount must be greater than 0\. |
| 60 | MSG60 | Toast (Success) | Voucher created | {voucher} {code} created. The balance has been updated. |
| 61 | MSG61 | Toast (Error) | Report generation failure | Unable to generate the report. Please try again. |
| 62 | MSG62 | Toast (Info) | No search results | No matching records were found. |
| 63 | MSG63 | Toast (Info) | Reorder point alert | {n} item(s) have reached or fallen below the reorder point. |
| 64 | MSG64 | Toast (Info) | Expiry alert | {n} lot(s) are expiring soon or have expired. |
| 65 | MSG65 | Toast (Error) | System processing error | The system could not complete the request. Please try again later. |
| 66 | MSG66 | Toast (Error) | New bookings paused | The system is not accepting new bookings (Order Settings). |
| 67 | MSG67 | Toast (Error) | Duplicate submission | The transaction is being processed. Please do not click Pay repeatedly. |
| 68 | MSG68 | Inline (Error) | Invalid price book | The price book is invalid: check the validity dates, branches, customers and the formula (a price book cannot take its price from itself or create a loop). |
| 69 | MSG69 | Inline (Error) | Plan quantity exceeded | The quantity to order exceeds the remaining quantity of the production plan. |
| 70 | MSG70 | Toast (Error) | Plan has active orders | The plan has production orders that are not cancelled. Cancel those orders or close the plan. |
| 71 | MSG71 | Inline (Error) | Invalid debt adjustment | The new debt value equals the current balance, the time is in the future or the description is longer than 500 characters. |
| 72 | MSG72 | Toast (Success) | Goods imported | {n} new products imported and {m} products updated successfully. |
| 73 | MSG73 | Toast (Error) | Order settings permission | Only the Admin can change the order settings and transaction rules. |
| 74 | MSG74 | Inline (Error) | Production order must follow BOM | The production order must follow the active BOM. To change the norms, update the BOM first. |

### **5.3 Assumptions & Out of Scope** {#5.3-assumptions-&-out-of-scope}

* **Users:** only office staff use StockFlow (Admin, Manager, Sales / Warehouse / Production Accountant). Field staff work on paper and report counted quantities; the system records only confirmed, physically counted figures (batch entry, not real time).

* **Approvals:** credit, production plan, stocktake and disposal decisions are recorded in StockFlow by the Manager (Chief Accountant). When company policy requires, the Manager consults the Director outside the system before recording the decision.

* **Credit:** there is no customer credit ranking and no interest on debt; credit limits and exceptions are decided case by case by the Manager.

* **Out of scope:** barcode/QR scanning devices, mobile/tablet applications, machine monitoring (OEE, speed, temperature), material consumption logging by workers, VAT calculation and electronic invoicing, integration with MISA or other accounting software, payroll and HR, delivery/vehicle management, design department documents.

* **Payment QR:** the payment QR code is only displayed for the customer to scan; StockFlow does not connect to the bank, so the Sales Accountant confirms the payment manually with the bank reference.
